research_question: How can record-augmentation techniques (MOVE.1) be applied using long-term continuous streamgages on Kaua'i to estimate natural low-flow availability (flow-duration discharges) at ungaged or partial-record sites?

phase_1.user_prompt: I am designing a surface water availability study for streams on Kaua'i, Hawaii. I need to identify long-term continuous streamgages on the windward side of the island to use as index stations for flow-duration analysis. Specifically, please find the USGS site numbers for the streamgages on Halaulani Stream and the left branch of 'Opaeka'a Stream. Also, what is the standard USGS 5-digit parameter code for discharge?

phase_2.user_prompt: Using the two index streamgages identified on Halaulani Stream and the left branch of 'Opaeka'a Stream, retrieve their daily mean discharge data for a 51-year base period spanning water years 1961 through 2011 (October 1, 1960, to September 30, 2011).

phase_3.user_prompt: Process the daily discharge data for the index stations to compute their 50th percentile (median) flow-duration discharges over the 1961-2011 base period. Because water management in Hawaii often relies on million gallons per day (Mgal/d), convert your computed percentiles from cubic feet per second (cfs) to Mgal/d. What is the calculated median discharge (Q50) for the Halaulani Stream station?

phase_4.user_prompt: To estimate median flow at an ungaged site on a nearby stream, we will use the Maintenance of Variance Extension Type 1 (MOVE.1) record-augmentation technique. We conducted several low-flow discharge measurements at the ungaged site and paired them with the concurrent daily mean discharge from the Halaulani Stream index station. The paired (Index, Ungaged) measurements in Mgal/d are: [(3.9, 2.50), (3.4, 1.51), (3.7, 2.01), (3.3, 1.50), (4.3, 2.86), (5.7, 2.92), (4.1, 1.66), (3.1, 1.36), (2.6, 0.80)]. First, convert both sets of values to base-10 logarithms. Compute the MOVE.1 regression relation in log-space. Finally, apply this relation to the index station's log-transformed base period Q50 (from the previous step, roughly 4.6 Mgal/d) to estimate the Q50 for the ungaged site. Convert your final answer back to linear space and provide the estimated Q50 in Mgal/d.
